author: La Touche, 1922
habitat: 서해 섬의 숲, 도시의 공원과 나무
summary: 중국 중부와 북부의 산지 숲에서만 번식하는 솔새로, 우리나라에서는 2004년 10월 소청도에서 처음 기록된 뒤 2020년 5월 백령도, 2025년 12월 인천 미추홀구 등에서 기록된 길잃은새다. 노랑허리솔새처럼 나뭇가지 끝의 잎 사이를 옮겨 다니며 곤충을 잡지만 그보다 덜 부산하다. 겨울은 중국 윈난 남부와 타이·미얀마·라오스 북부에서 나는 것으로 알려져 있다.

points.en: faint pale median crown stripe, weak toward the bill

similar.how: 노랑허리솔새보다 전체가 칙칙하고 부리가 가늘며, 머리 가운데 선이 이마 쪽에서 흐려지고 허리의 노란 띠가 작고 흐리다.

art.subject: Chinese Leaf Warbler (Phylloscopus yunnanensis), adult (sexes alike) in spring: a pale greyish-yellow median crown stripe, diffuse and fading towards the forehead, between greyish-olive lateral crown stripes; a long, well-defined whitish supercilium with no yellow tinge, a little buffier towards the rear; a dark olive eye-stripe; rather plain ear-coverts; upperparts olive-green with a pale yellowish-white band across the rump; wings dark with two yellowish-white wing-bars, the lower one more distinct, and pale-edged tertials; underparts whitish with a faint yellowish tinge; fine dark bill with a pale base to the lower mandible; dark eye; very dark brown, almost blackish legs.
art.pose: flitting among pine twigs, side view, wings slightly drooped to show the pale rump band
art.scene: pine and deciduous woodland on a Korean offshore island during spring migration in April or May, soft light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view among pine twigs, wings slightly drooped: faint pale median crown stripe between dusky-olive lateral crown stripes, pale supercilium without yellow, dark eye-stripe, olive-green upperparts, pale yellowish-white rump, distinct greater-covert bar and fainter median-covert bar, whitish-edged tertials, whitish underparts, dark legs

adult, head detail in side view: faint pale median crown stripe fading toward the forehead and not reaching the bill, dusky-olive lateral crown stripes, well-defined pale supercilium without yellow, dark eye-stripe, fine short bill, dark with a paler base below
art.build: A tiny, compact leaf warbler, smaller than a sparrow and about the size of a Yellow-browed Warbler, only slightly larger than a Pallas's Leaf Warbler; large-headed and short-tailed. Bill fine and short, much shorter than the head. Legs slender and very dark. Tail short and square, often flicked. Very active in the outer foliage, sometimes hovering briefly at leaf tips, which shows the pale rump band.
avoid: Do not paint a sharp lemon-yellow crown stripe and bright lemon rump between blackish crown stripes; that is Pallas's Leaf Warbler (Phylloscopus proregulus).
Do not omit the pale yellow rump band or the two wing-bars.
Do not paint bright yellow underparts; they are whitish.
Do not paint a large, long-tailed warbler; it is tiny and short-tailed.
Do not paint pale pinkish legs or a yellow front to the supercilium; the legs are very dark and the supercilium is whitish throughout.
